message.content:
**Traffic Laws & Regulations – State of Texas** Below is a quick‑reference guide covering the most common rules you’ll encounter on Texas roads. For full legal text consult the *Texas Transportation Code* (TTC), the *Texas Administrative Code*, or the Texas Department of Public Safety’s (DPS) “Driver Handbook” online. | Topic | Key Rules / Limits | Notes | |-------|--------------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Rural interstate/highway: **55 mph** (unless posted <55)
• Urban freeways: up to **70–75 mph** depending on county
• Residential streets: usually **25–35 mph**
• School zones: **20 mph** during school hours | Posted signs override default limits. Always obey local signage. | | **Seat Belts & Child Restraints** | • All passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children ≤ 8 years old or weighing < 80 lb must ride in a federally approved child restraint appropriate for their size.
• Back‑seat children > 8 yrs who weigh ≥ 80 lb may use seat belt alone.| Failure to buckle can result in a $50 fine plus possible points. | | **Cell Phone Use** | • Holding a hand‑held cellphone while driving is prohibited.
• Using a hands‑free device (e.g., Bluetooth headset, speakerphone) is permitted.
• Texting while driving is disallowed regardless of device type.| Violations carry a base fine of $100 + potential points. | | **Alcohol Impairment** | • BAC ≥ 0.08 % for adults → DUI offense.
• Zero‑tolerance (< 0.02 %) applies to anyone under 21.
• Penalties: fines ($1k+), license revocation, mandatory education programs, possible incarceration. | First offenses often involve a suspended license and a court‑ordered program. Repeat offenders face harsher sanctions. | | **Driving Under Influence of Drugs** | • Prescription drugs that impair driving count toward DUI.
• Illicit drug possession while driving is a separate felony charge. | Courts consider medical records and blood tests. | | **Points System** | • Most moving violations add 2–5 points to your record.
• Accumulating 12 points within 36 months triggers a license review and possible suspension.
• Certain serious infractions (e.g., reckless driving) automatically suspend licenses. | Insurance companies track points; more points raise premiums. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles approaching from the left yield to those coming straight ahead.
• Pedestrians always have priority where crosswalks exist.
• Stop signs require a complete stop even if no other cars present. | Failing to yield can incur both a ticket and liability for damages. | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlamps must be used between sunset/sunrise and whenever visibility drops below 500 ft.
• Fog lights are restricted to foggy conditions. | Improper lighting can cause a citation and increased risk of accidents. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep inside lane unless passing or turning.
• Do not weave across lanes (“lane splitting”) unless overtaking another vehicle. | Lane discipline violations are typically treated as careless driving. | | **School Bus Stops** | • Vehicles traveling eastbound must stop one side of the bus; westbound—other side.
• Must remain stopped until the bus driver signals it’s safe to proceed. | Ignoring this rule carries heavy fines and points. | --- ### Where to Find Official Sources | Resource | What It Offers | How To Access | |----------|---------------|--------------| | **Texas DPS Driver Handbooks** | Full statutes, diagrams, practice questions | https://www.dps.texas.gov/section/drivers-license-and-identification-card/dl-handbook | | **Texas Transportation Code (Title 7)** | Legal code governing road safety | https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/?link=TTc | | **Texas DOT Roadside Assistance** | Quick reference for emergencies | https://www.txdot.gov/travelers.html | | **Local County Clerk Websites** | Specific municipal ordinances (speed limits, parking restrictions) | Search “[County] city council minutes” | --- #### Practical Tips for Safe Driving in Texas 1. **Always Check Signage:** Even though state defaults exist, many counties post different limits. 2. **Use Your GPS Wisely:** Many navigation apps now flag Texas-specific rules (e.g., no texting). 3. **Keep Documentation Handy:** Carry proof of insurance, registration, and valid driver's license. 4. **Plan Ahead for Weather:** Winter storms can reduce traction dramatically; adjust speeds accordingly. 5. **Know Your Local Ordinances:** Some cities impose stricter seat‑belt enforcement or additional fines. Feel free to let me know if you’d like deeper detail on any particular area—such as commercial trucking regulations, toll‑road requirements, or how to contest a ticket!
